title: Seamless kernel binding and ABI compatibility layer for CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS upgrades
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Recent upgrades to CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS (moving towards CUDA 13 + Triton 3 in some infra images) have surfaced multiple ABI and symbol-level incompatibilities in our kernel selection layer. Symptoms observed: broken kernel bindings at runtime, silent fallback to suboptimal kernels, and occasional cuBLAS workspace errors causing transient OOM-like failures. These issues have caused failed deployments for a small subset of dedicated clusters and increased tail latency during exemplar workloads.

Proposal: Implement an ABI compatibility shim and a dynamic kernel-binding registry that supports version negotiation and graceful fallback. The shim will:
- Detect loaded CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS versions at runtime and normalize symbol names/entry points where necessary.
- Provide a kernel capability table: per-kernel metadata (architecture, CUTLASS version, required cublas/cuops behavior) that the runtime can query to pick a compatible kernel binary.
- Fall back deterministically: preferred compiled kernel -> ABI-shim resolved kernel -> compatible older kernel variant -> CPU or reference path (with explicit telemetry and rate-limiting).
- Expose a feature-flagged runtime knob to force strict compatibility (fail-fast) for safety during canaries.

Scope / Non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on runtime-side compatibility (binding/lookup/fallback and tests). We will not attempt to rebuild or recompile every kernel in this ticket (that is follow-on work: ENG-16043). We also won't change customer-visible defaults except via controlled rollout.

Implementation plan:
1) Compatibility detector: lightweight probe that inspects CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS runtime symbols and reports a normalized version string and capability flags.
2) Kernel registry and manifest format: small extensible JSON manifest per kernel shipped with metadata for negotiation. Manifest format documented in /confluence/gpu/manifest.
3) ABI shims: encapsulated translation layer for the most common symbol mismatches discovered during triage (name mangling, parameter order changes). Add tests that load both old and new runtime stacks.
4) Runtime integration: query registry during kernel selection and preferred-fallback logic. Add instrumentation for selection decision tree.
5) Tests: microbenchmarks (latency/throughput), integration e2e using production request traces, fuzzing for symbol mismatch cases.
6) Rollout: feature-flag off by default; enable for internal canary clusters -> 10% dedicated -> 50% -> GA behind runtime-1.25.

Success metrics:
- Zero customer-facing regressions in canary clusters (errors attributed to kernel incompatibilities decrease to 0).
- No more silent fallbacks: selection telemetry shows explicit fallback events < 0.1% of requests.
- Tail latency (p99) regression < 5% compared to baseline on representative workloads.

Risks & mitigations:
- Performance overhead from indirection in the compatibility shim. Mitigation: microbench and optimize hot paths; provide opt-out compile-time flag.
- Unanticipated symbol mismatches. Mitigation: shipping robust translation table and a fallback to CPU reference path.
- Increased binary size / maintenance. Mitigation: keep shim small and gated behind feature flags; document for downstream kernel teams.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/Kernel+ABI+Compatibility+Shim
- Design doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2876
- Prototype PR (shim + registry): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2914
- Perf dashboard (benchmark suite): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/GPUPERF/kernel-compat

Next steps (current sprint):
- Land compatibility detector (Avery) and basic manifest schema (Diego) by 2026-02-28.
- Merge prototype shim into feature branch, add unit tests and a small canary image by 2026-03-07.
- Start controlled canary on two internal dedicated clusters by 2026-03-12.
